profile.entities: KNR Constructions Limited; KNR Ramanattukara Infra Private Limited; KNR Guruvayur Infra Private Limited
profile.themes: NHAI reform momentum; HAM project completion; State highway bidding surge; Mining project development

bull_bear.body: Priority: debt reduction (net debt/equity 0.49x); HAM equity infusion (INR175cr FY26); mining development capex (INR30-40cr); potential asset monetization of 4 HAM assets (SPA draft circulated, deal expected by Nov 2025 end)
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delayed state government payments (INR1,350cr receivables, INR677cr from Kaleshwaram P4); NHAI bidding freeze until Nov 30, 2025; land acquisition delays in mining (Odisha) and highway projects (Mysore-Kushalnagara P5); aggressive bidding in state tenders; potential write-offs if receivables not cleared by Q1FY27
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges worst order inflow period in history but confident in NHAI revival post-Nov 2025; proactive on receivables (repeated ministerial meetings); focused on execution, cost control, and diversification into mining/solar
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: INR150-200cr of unbilled irrigation revenue expected to be certified in Q3FY26; mining project's INR90cr development phase revenue is non-recurring and will not impact EBITDA margin; asset monetization of 4 HAM assets could reduce net debt by INR500-700cr if closed by Dec 2025
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Standalone balance sheet has been effectively debt-free with Debt-to-Equity of 0.00 every year from FY21 through FY26, versus a peak of 0.25 in FY10.
- Standalone Net Worth grew from ₹3,008 Mn (FY10) to ₹40,548 Mn (FY26).
- Active capital-recycling via asset monetization: completed transfer of KNR Palani Infra (invested ~₹64 Cr, consideration ₹295 Cr incl. ₹90 Cr cash surplus) and KNR Ramagiri Infra (invested ₹83 Cr, consideration ₹227 Cr) to Indus Infra Trust.
- Broader monetization plan covers 4 SPVs (KNR Palani, KNR Ramagiri, KNR Guruvayur, KNR Ramanattukara) with total equity invested of ₹5,567 Mn against total consideration of ₹15,597 Mn (2.5x-4.6x across the SPVs), expected to complete on or before 30 September 2026.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Road: INR2,537cr order book; Irrigation: INR1,540cr (INR720cr unbilled); Mining: INR3,597cr (Odisha bid INR1,200cr pending); Pipeline: INR1,049cr; Urban flyovers: INR531cr (Hyderabad projects won); HAM: 8 projects, 5 nearing completion (95%+), 2 with delays (Mysore-Kushalnagara P5)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delayed state government payments | IRB Infra | loser | Medium | Similar exposure to state receivables; KNR's aggressive collection may pressure peers to follow suit, increasing sector-wide liquidity stress |
| NHAI bidding freeze until Nov 30, 2025 | GMR Infrastructure | beneficiary | Low | Larger players may benefit more from NHAI's post-November tender surge due to stronger balance sheets |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- One of the leading EPC players in Roads & Highways with established presence in Irrigation and Urban Water Infrastructure Management; 30+ years of execution experience, ~9,127 lane km of road projects completed across 12 states.
- Credit ratings reaffirmed by CRISIL: Long Term Bank Facilities at CRISIL AA (Stable) and Short Term ratings at CRISIL A1+ (Stable).
- Founder-promoter-led management — Mr. K. Narasimha Reddy (Managing Director, 50+ years in the Highway sector) and Mr. K. Jalandhar Reddy (Executive Director, 25+ years) — supported by a professional team spanning projects, finance and compliance.
- New vertical entry: Letter of Acceptance from South Eastern Coalfields Limited for coal mining and overburden removal at Kusmunda OCP, Chhattisgarh (JV with Sushee Infra & Mining Limited), marking expansion beyond the traditional roads/irrigation base.
- Strong order book of ₹86,674 Mn as on 30 June 2026, split Roads ₹25,977 Mn, Irrigation & Pipeline ₹25,173 Mn and Mining ₹35,524 Mn.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: - [Shareholding] As of 30 June 2026: Promoters 48.81%, Public & Others 28.46%, Mutual Funds/AIFs/Insurance Cos. 17.30%, Foreign Institutional Investors 5.43%; largest non-promoter holders include ICICI Prudential MF (4.73%), Invesco MF (4.11%) and HDFC MF (3.76%).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin 29.8% consolidated (H1), down from 31.2% H1 FY25 due to INR20cr one-offs (director pay + Ramanattukara provision); core margin remains ~32%; mining margins expected 18-20% in operation phase; irrigation margins pressured by delayed payments
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: INR2,000cr H2 FY26; Margin: 13-14% EBITDA; Order inflow: INR8,000-10,000cr by FY26 end; Capex/commissioning: INR30-40cr for FY26, mostly for mining development; No new HAM equity infusion beyond INR175cr FY26 and INR117cr FY27
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR8,748cr total; Road: 29%; Irrigation: 18%; Mining: 41%; Pipeline: 12%; 81% third-party (76% state, 3% central, 2% private); 19% captive HAM; 1.5-2 year execution horizon excluding mining
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Entry into solar energy projects via new CEO hire; potential EPC partnerships with IRB and Cube; mining project operational phase (INR300-400cr/year revenue from Year 2); irrigation and state highway expansion in MP, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: KNR Constructions is transitioning from a low-execution phase to a recovery phase, with HAM projects nearing completion and new EPC orders in Telangana providing near-term revenue visibility; the key catalyst is the resolution of delayed receivables and order inflow from NHAI post-November 2025.
